signals.title: CAD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Monetary Divergence
signals.text: CAD/JPY is the dominant bilateral theme of the week as CAD outperforms with a +0.609% average while JPY lags at -0.685%, creating a significant 1.294% spread across G10 peers. The move is underpinned by a 125bp OIS carry advantage for the Loonie (BoC CORRA 2.30% vs BoJ TONA 0.98%) and a constructive CAD ESI at +12.0. While JPY bond yields are rising on BoJ hike expectations, Japan's fiscal concerns and the current risk-on backdrop—evidenced by the Nikkei's 2.08% rally and VIX at 15.2—keep the JPY under pressure. The pair currently benefits from BoC data outperformance and JPY being used as a primary funding currency in a low-volatility regime. Trade bias: Bullish CAD/JPY; yield-seeking flows and fiscal headwinds for JPY sustain the divergence. Catalyst: BoC meeting 9 Sep — 100% hold priced. Risk: Sharp risk-off deleveraging spikes JPY safe-haven demand, compressing the G10 spread below 0.80%.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Geopolitical Risk + Options Skew Divergence
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 158.91, positioned below its SMA20/50/200 cluster following recent post-NFP dollar weakness. Despite a massive 275bp Fed-BoJ carry advantage (Fed 3.75% vs BoJ 1.0%), the options market is pricing in heavy downside protection with a 1M 25d Risk Reversal of -2.18. BoJ holds at 1.0%. While carry typically dominates when VIX is at 15.2, the negative 1.3% Vol Risk Premium indicates the options market is currently underpricing realized volatility, suggesting a potential for sharp, unexpected moves if the geopolitical situation worsens. Trade bias: Neutral USD/JPY; carry advantage is increasingly offset by extreme options hedging and geopolitical risk. Catalyst: US CPI on Wednesday. Risk: A clean break back above the SMA200 at 158.07 validates carry dominance and forces an unwind of yen-denominated hedges.

signals.title: NZD/USD — ESI Outperformance + Short Squeeze Setup
signals.text: NZD/USD at 0.5893 holds above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.5790–0.5836) following a sustained run of data beats, reflected in a G10-leading ESI of +24.4. This fundamental strength stands in direct opposition to speculative positioning, where COT LF net remains heavily short at -30,785 (only 9.7% long). The RBNZ's hiking stance and a negative real rate of -1.56% continue to provide a hawkish policy floor that specs are currently fading. Retail sentiment also shows a 77% short bias, aligning with institutional shorts and creating a high-conviction environment for a contrarian squeeze higher if US CPI underwhelms. Trade bias: Long NZD/USD; data-led outperformance against a crowded spec short creates asymmetric upside. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting 2 Sep — hike priced. Risk: US CPI surprise to the upside revitalizes the USD, validating the existing spec short.

signals.title: AUD/USD — CB Carry + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7067, supported by a 60bp carry advantage over the USD (RBA 4.35% vs Fed 3.75%). Speculative positioning remains net long (+37,990), but retail traders have moved to a 78% short extreme, fading the recent 1M rally of +1.89%. This divergence typically favors institutional direction, especially with the AUD holding above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.6925–0.7002). While AUD ESI is soft at -12.2, the 1W G10 average performance of +0.370% suggests the currency is successfully weathering local data misses due to the high carry profile. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/USD; institutional longs and carry support likely to force retail capitulation. Catalyst: RBA meeting 11 Aug — hold priced. Risk: RBA adopts a surprisingly dovish tone, removing the carry floor and triggering a long unwind toward 0.6925.

signals.title: USD/NOK — Retail Extreme + Policy Floor
signals.text: USD/NOK retail sentiment has reached a 100% long extreme, marking an absolute consensus among retail participants for a USD bounce. This extreme contrarian signal occurs while the Norges Bank maintains a restrictive policy stance with a 4.25% rate and a +1.51% real rate, providing structural support for the Krone. USD/NOK is currently trading below its SMA20/50/200 cluster (9.60–9.70), confirming a bearish technical regime. Given the 100% retail long positioning, the pair faces significant downside risk as any further NOK strength will likely trigger forced liquidations of these retail positions. Trade bias: Bearish USD/NOK; contrarian to 100% retail long extreme with support from restrictive NOK real rates. Catalyst: NOK meeting 13 Aug — hold priced. Risk: A sharp reversal in WTI oil prices (currently $80.8) weakens the NOK fundamental floor and relieves retail pressure.
